newsitem.title: USA: Paxson near deal to buy TV station - sources.
newsitem.headline: Paxson near deal to buy TV station - sources.

text.p: Paxson Communications Corp is expected to announce as early as next week that it will buy New York's WBIS television station from ITT Corp and Dow Jones & Co Inc for $250 million, according to sources familiar with the negotiations.
Paxson is working this week to line up definitive financing for the deal. The transaction will not take place unless the financing is in place, the sources said.
"There is a handshake (agreement) for a deal at $250 million," said one source who did not want to be identified.
ITT and Dow Jones jointly bought WBIS for $207 million from the city of New York in 1995. The station's business news and sports format has not gained a strong following among viewers.
Dow Jones declined to comment on the sale of WBIS.
ITT also declined to comment, although President Robert Bowman said during a conference call Tuesday that the company had received considerable interest in the station.
Paxson could not be reached for comment. The company owns, operates or is affiliated with 47 television stations and reaches 53.4 million households.
The value of WBIS was solidified recently after the Supreme Court last month upheld a 1992 law that forces cable television operators to carry local station broadcasts.
For Paxson, the acquisition of a New York station would represent a big step in its strategy of entering major U.S. markets. The company also owns radio stations, mostly in Florida.
Upon announcing a sale of WBIS, ITT will still have a handful of valuable assets to sell. The company owns an international telephone directories business and an educational services unit.

ITT, which is selling the assets to focus on its core hotel and casino businesses, has not announced what it might do with the proceeds of the asset sales. Many industry experts expect the company to issue a special dividend or institute a stock buyback.
